title: GraphRAG methods to create optimized LLM context windows for Retrieval — Jonathan Larson, Microsoft
talk_summary: Jonathan Larson presents GraphRAG for code: building graph structures over repositories to answer local/global questions, translate code, generate docs, and enable multi-file feature work by a coding agent. He also announces Benchmark QED for auto-generating local/global queries and LLM-judge evaluation, and claims lazy graph retrieval beats vector RAG at lower cost than 1M-token context.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build a graph of code entities and relationships, then retrieve local neighborhoods or global module summaries instead of dumping raw files into context.
takeaways.numbers: 200 lines/7 files; Doom 100k lines/231 files; raw LLM translation failed, GraphRAG translation ran

takeaways.what_they_do: Use the graph to pull changed symbols' dependents and call sites plus module context into review, not just the diff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it changed a whole lot of files and it worked out of the box
takeaways.numbers: Doom 100k lines/231 files; multi-file jump feature worked where other agents failed

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate local/global and data/persona-driven questions over a dataset, then use an LLM judge to score answers on comprehensiveness, diversity, empowerment, and relevance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: auto Q is focused on doing query generation for target data sets

takeaways.technique: Graph retrieval instead of long context
takeaways.what_they_do: Retrieve structured graph context rather than stuffing a 1M-token window; the vendor claims lazy graph wins at one-tenth the cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: lazy graph was a tenth of the cost of what we saw in the 1 million token context windows
takeaways.numbers: 92%, 90%, 91% wins vs vector RAG at 8K/120K/1M; 1/10 cost of 1M context

takeaways.technique: Generated module docs as shared memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Use global queries to generate repository/module documentation, then local queries to drill into individual files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: looking at modules in their entirety like across 20 30 files

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose GraphRAG as a backend service that a coding agent calls to form a holistic plan.
takeaways.evidence_quote: GitHub copilot coding agent reaching out to graph for code on the back end
